correctness.rationale: Directly transform the target CDF with A=log(alpha), ell=log(A), theta_j=e^{-s_j}/A, beta_j=c_j/ell. Uniform elementary Taylor expansion on compact rectangles yields the nondegenerate discrete Fréchet CDF exp(-e^{-s_j}(x+1)^{-c_j}). Every observed finite PMF, survivor and upper-record transition remains bounded away from zero. The exact reciprocal-prior Jacobian is 1/(c1 c2); restricting to compact s,c yields an infinite dA integral. The packaged actual-path numerical checks verify the CDF and both likelihood limits and a symbolic Jacobian determinant. No finite experiment substitutes for the analytical divergence proof.

originality.rationale: No checked published result covers the five-parameter DAPW-specific boundary or the resulting universal posterior impropriety. The 2026 primary article supplies the PMF and improper joint prior but asserts informative data usually make such posteriors proper; its earlier DAPW distribution paper has no matching prior-normalization analysis. The rigorously closest continuous Weibull propriety theorem instead has a different likelihood geometry and cannot imply this boundary. Targeted published-result and external literature searches covered the exact DOI, the prior, proper-posterior aliases, discrete Fréchet limit, and joint-parameter escape.

value.rationale: The source treats Bayesian posterior means, credible intervals, and a claimed empirical advantage of Bayes estimates as central outcomes under two data regimes. Its stated joint improper prior has no finite posterior normalizer for ANY finite valid data, even abundant diverse records, because an escaping nondegenerate family preserves likelihood. This structural obstruction cannot be cured by more finite observations or ordinary numeric integration; a changed prior/domain is required. The finding distinguishes the excluded fixed-alpha mixed-record design and makes no unsupported code-level assertion.
